title: Adverbs and the も particle
summary: Three ways to make an adverb, the experience pattern たことがない, and も, the topic flag that means "also".

blocks.text: An adverb describes the **engine**: how, how fast, how suddenly. Japanese has three common ways to make one.

blocks.jp: うさぎは早く走って、急に穴に飛び込んだ。
blocks.en: The rabbit ran fast and suddenly jumped into a hole.

blocks.jp: でも驚いたことに、ゆっくり落ちた。
blocks.en: But, surprisingly, she fell very slowly.

blocks.text: **〜ことに** after an emotion word (驚いた, 嬉しい) is a ready-made adverb meaning "to my surprise / happily".

**〜たことがある / ない** means "have / have never done". The grammatical subject is **こと** (a matter), not the person. The person can only be the topic with は: "as for me, the matter of having seen it does not exist".

blocks.jp: 私は話すうさぎを見たことがない。
blocks.en: I have never seen a talking rabbit.

blocks.text: **も** is the second non-logical particle, like **は**. It replaces は when the new topic does **the same thing** as the one before: "also". It needs an earlier topic to refer to. Compare three versions after the rabbit jumped in:

blocks.jp: アリスはうさぎの穴に飛び込んだ。
blocks.en: Alice jumped into the rabbit hole. (は: Alice, in contrast to the rabbit)

blocks.jp: アリスがうさぎの穴に飛び込んだ。
blocks.en: Alice jumped into the rabbit hole. (が: a plain statement of who)

blocks.jp: アリスもうさぎの穴に飛び込んだ。
blocks.en: Alice also jumped into the rabbit hole.

items: **い → く**: 早く. **Noun + に**: 急に. **Alone**: ゆっくり.
**〜たことがない**: never have; the subject is こと.
**も** = "also", and it replaces は or が when the new topic does the same thing.
